units.explain: Normalizes a PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME-style value: None and timedelta inputs pass through unchanged; any int (or other non-timedelta) is interpreted as seconds and converted via timedelta(seconds=value). Used as the get_converter of the permanent_session_lifetime ConfigAttribute. Pure function, no side effects.
units.summary: Converts an int seconds value into a timedelta; passes None/timedelta through.
uncertainties: Non-int non-timedelta values would still be passed to timedelta(seconds=...); resulting TypeError is not handled here.

units.explain: Sans-IO application core subclassing Scaffold: a central registry for URL rules, blueprints, error handlers, Jinja configuration, and extension state. Class attributes define pluggable classes (aborter_class, jinja_environment, app_ctx_globals_class, config_class, url_rule_class, url_map_class, json_provider_class) and ConfigAttribute descriptors (testing->TESTING, secret_key->SECRET_KEY, permanent_session_lifetime->PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME with _make_timedelta converter). jinja_options is a plain mutable dict read when the Jinja environment is first created; later changes have no effect. should_ignore_error is a deprecated None-valued placeholder. Concrete request handling lives in flask/app.py's Flask subclass; create_jinja_environment is abstract here. The class body is split in the inventory (s0 attributes/docs, s32 the deprecated should_ignore_error region), both covered by this unit.
units.summary: Sans-IO Flask application core holding routing, config, blueprint, and Jinja registries with pluggable class hooks.
uncertainties: Runtime effects of ConfigAttribute descriptors depend on flask/config.py, not shown here.

extras.note: jinja_options must be set before first access of jinja_env; afterwards changes are ignored.

units.explain: Initializes the app: delegates resource/static/template/root_path setup to Scaffold.__init__, then resolves the instance path — auto-detected via auto_find_instance_path when not given, ValueError if a relative path is supplied. Builds config via make_config(instance_relative_config), the aborter via make_aborter, and the JSON provider instance. Initializes empty registries: url_build_error_handlers, teardown_appcontext_funcs, shell_context_processors, blueprints (insertion-ordered dict), extensions. Creates url_map from url_map_class(host_matching=host_matching), stores subdomain_matching, and sets _got_first_request=False, which later gates setup methods. No returns; exceptions: ValueError for relative instance_path, plus whatever Scaffold/find_package raise.
units.summary: Constructor resolving instance path and initializing config, aborter, JSON provider, and empty registries.

extras.note: A relative instance_path argument raises ValueError immediately.

units.explain: Guard used by setup methods: raises AssertionError if _got_first_request is True, i.e. once the app has handled its first request, registration-time mutation (routes, blueprints, template hooks) is refused because changes would no longer apply consistently. No-op otherwise.
units.summary: Raises AssertionError if setup methods run after the first request was handled.

units.explain: Cached property returning the application display name. If import_name is '__main__', the name is derived from the __main__ module's __file__ (basename without extension); if that file is unknown it falls back to the literal '__main__'. Otherwise returns import_name. Cached, so later changes to import_name or __main__.__file__ are not reflected.
units.summary: Application display name; derived from the run file when import_name is __main__.

units.explain: Cached property returning a standard logging.Logger for the app, created by flask.logging.create_logger(self) and named after the app. Level/handler setup (debug level, default handler when none configured) is delegated to create_logger, which is outside this file; per the docstring the level is only set at creation time.
units.summary: Lazily created per-app logger via create_logger, named after the app.
uncertainties: Exact handler/level behavior lives in flask/logging.py, not visible here.

units.explain: Cached property that builds the Jinja environment on first access by calling create_jinja_environment() (implemented by the concrete subclass; in this sansio class it raises NotImplementedError). Because it is cached, jinja_options and related attributes must be configured before the first access to have any effect.
units.summary: Lazily creates and caches the Jinja environment on first access.
uncertainties: What create_jinja_environment assembles is defined in flask/app.py, not in this file.

units.explain: Constructs the config object: root path is instance_path when instance_relative is True, otherwise self.root_path. Copies class-level default_config into a dict, overrides DEBUG from the environment via get_debug_flag(), and instantiates config_class(root_path, defaults). Called only from __init__.
units.summary: Builds the Config object with defaults and environment-derived DEBUG.

units.explain: Factory for the app's aborter: returns aborter_class() (default werkzeug Aborter). The resulting object is stored as self.aborter and invoked by flask.abort; subclasses can swap aborter_class or override this factory.
units.summary: Creates the app's Aborter instance from aborter_class.

units.explain: Locates the instance folder when none was supplied: calls find_package(import_name); if no installation prefix is found, returns '<package_path>/instance', otherwise '<prefix>/var/<name>-instance' using the cached name property. Path resolution depends on find_package (scaffold.py).
units.summary: Auto-detects the instance folder next to the package or under var/ when prefixed.

units.explain: Returns a DispatchingJinjaLoader(self) that dispatches template loading between the app's own loader and registered blueprints' loaders. Docstring discourages overriding this; subclasses should override jinja_loader instead.
units.summary: Creates the dispatching Jinja loader covering app and blueprint templates.

units.explain: Autoescape policy: returns True when filename is None; otherwise case-insensitively checks the extension against .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml, .svg. Extensions outside that set get autoescaping disabled. Pure predicate.
units.summary: Enables autoescape for None names and HTML/XML/SVG extensions, case-insensitively.

units.explain: Getter/setter pair over the DEBUG config key. The getter simply returns config['DEBUG']. The setter writes the value into config and, if TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD is still None (unset), mirrors the value onto the (creating it if needed) jinja_env.auto_reload. Because jinja_env is cached, setting debug after the environment exists changes its auto_reload but not any other environment options.
units.summary: Debug flag mapped to the DEBUG config key; setter syncs Jinja auto-reload when unset.
uncertainties: Side effect triggers environment creation if jinja_env was not yet accessed.

units.explain: Setter half of the debug property; explained with the getter unit.
units.summary: Setter for the debug property.

units.explain: Setup-method-guarded registration of a Blueprint: records options and delegates to blueprint.register(self, options), which (in blueprints.py) applies url_prefix/subdomain/url_defaults and adds the blueprint's rules to this app. Keyword options override blueprint defaults and are passed through to BlueprintSetupState; the 'name' option lets the same blueprint be registered multiple times under distinct names. Mutates self.blueprints via the callee. The guard forbids registration after the first request.
units.summary: Registers a blueprint, delegating rule setup to Blueprint.register.

relations.basis: registration populates self.blueprints, which iter_blueprints exposes

units.explain: Returns self.blueprints.values(), a ValuesView over registered blueprints in registration order; multiple registrations of the same blueprint under different names appear multiple times. Explained here and folded into the registration documentation.
units.summary: View over registered blueprints in registration order.

units.explain: Core route registration, guarded as a setup method. Derives the endpoint from the view function when omitted; pops 'methods' from options; falls back to view_func.methods or ('GET',); rejects a bare string with TypeError; uppercases and set-ifies methods. Computes required_methods from view_func.required_methods; resolves provide_automatic_options (explicit arg > view_func attribute > OPTIONS not already in methods and config PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS), adding 'OPTIONS' to required methods when automatic options apply, then unions required methods in. Instantiates url_rule_class(rule, methods=methods, **options), sets provide_automatic_options on the rule, and adds it to url_map. Finally registers the view function: raises AssertionError if the endpoint already maps to a different function, otherwise stores it.
units.summary: Creates a URL rule, resolves methods/automatic OPTIONS, registers rule and view function.

relations.basis: @setupmethod guard applied to this route-registration method

extras.note: TypeError when methods is a string; AssertionError when reusing an endpoint with a different view function.
provide_automatic_options precedence: explicit argument, then view_func attribute, then config-derived default.

units.explain: Template hook registration API, three parallel families (filter, test, global), each with the same shape. The decorator form template_filter/template_test/template_global doubles as direct and parametrized: if called with a callable it registers immediately and returns the function (usable without parentheses); otherwise it returns a decorator closure that registers under the given name (or the function's __name__ when None). All paths funnel into add_template_filter/add_template_test/add_template_global, which are setup-method-guarded and write directly into the (possibly triggering creation of) cached jinja_env's filters/tests/globals dict: jinja_env.filters[name or f.__name__] = f (and .tests/.globals analogues). Registering after the first request violates the setup guard; registering after jinja_env was already created still works but only affects that cached environment. Overload stubs and inner decorator closures are covered by this unit.
units.summary: Decorator and direct registration of Jinja filters, tests, and globals into the cached jinja_env.

relations.basis: @setupmethod decorates add_template_filter/test/global and the template_* decorators

uncertainties: Behavior when the same name is registered twice is not checked here; last write wins in the Jinja dict.

units.explain: Setup-method-guarded decorator that appends f to teardown_appcontext_funcs and returns f unchanged. These functions run when the app context is popped (end of request, CLI command, or with-block exit); on unhandled exceptions they receive the error, otherwise None. Return values are ignored; raising from teardown is discouraged and not mitigated here. Setup is refused after the first request via the guard.
units.summary: Registers a teardown function for app-context pop and returns it unchanged.

units.explain: Setup-method-guarded decorator that appends f to shell_context_processors and returns f; processors supply variables when a flask shell context is created. Covered with the other registration decorators.
units.summary: Registers a shell context processor and returns it unchanged.

units.explain: Error-handler lookup for an exception given a candidate blueprint name list. Resolves (exc_class, code) via Scaffold._get_exc_class_and_code(type(e)); candidates are searched in precedence order: for each code in (code, None) when a code exists (else only None), for each name in (*blueprints, None) — i.e. most specific blueprint first, then app level — inspect error_handler_spec[name][c], skipping empty maps, and walk exc_class.__mro__ returning the first handler whose class key matches. Returns None if nothing matches. Behavior of error_handler_spec population lives in the concrete Flask subclass; whether self.get or dict.get applies is ambiguous in the graph and the dict-like mapping is assumed.
units.summary: Finds the most specific registered error handler by code, blueprint, and exception MRO.
uncertainties: Structure of error_handler_spec is defined in flask/app.py, not visible here; this reading assumes a nested {name: {code: {cls: handler}}} mapping.
Graph showed two candidates for handler_map.get(cls); treated as mapping lookup per the nested-spec reading.

units.explain: Decides whether an HTTP exception raised by a view should escape error handling and surface as a regular traceback. Returns True if config TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS is set. Otherwise, if TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is unset (None), debug mode is on, and the exception is a BadRequestKeyError, it is trapped. If TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is truthy, returns whether the exception is a BadRequest. Default: False (no trapping). Called by the concrete Flask exception-handling path.
units.summary: Determines if an HTTP exception is trapped for debugging instead of handled.

units.explain: Creates a redirect response by delegating to werkzeug's redirect with location, the given status code (default 303, changed from 302 in 3.2), and Response=self.response_class so the app's response class is used. Called by flask.redirect; raising/return semantics are werkzeug's.
units.summary: Builds a redirect response using the app's response class; default code 303.

relations.basis: uses self.response_class declared on the Scaffold/App class

uncertainties: response_class is only declared (type) in this file; its concrete assignment lives in flask/app.py.

units.explain: Implements inject_url_defaults for URL building (called from Flask.url_for): starts with name None (app-level defaults) and, when the endpoint contains a dot, chains the blueprint ancestors from _split_blueprint_path of the endpoint prefix in reversed order (most specific first), so url_for works outside a request context. For each name present in url_default_functions, calls each function with (endpoint, values), letting them mutate values in place. No return value.
units.summary: Applies app- and blueprint-level url default functions to the values dict before building a URL.
uncertainties: url_default_functions is populated elsewhere (concrete Flask class), not visible in this file.

units.explain: BuildError fallback for url_for. Iterates url_build_error_handlers, calling each with (error, endpoint, values). A handler raising BuildError has that new error captured into the loop variable (deliberately, so it is available outside the except block) and iteration continues; a handler returning None is skipped; the first non-None return value is returned to url_for. If no handler produces a value, the (possibly replaced) error is re-raised: bare `raise` when it is the currently active exception, otherwise `raise error`. Setup-method-free; callable at any time.
units.summary: Runs URL build error handlers; returns first result or re-raises the BuildError.

extras.note: A handler raising BuildError replaces the active error for subsequent handlers and the final raise.
Return value semantics: None from a handler means 'not handled'; any other value is returned by url_for.

payload.batch_notes: Single file batch. All 39 resolved call sites map to batch-visible relations; two graph ambiguities (handler_map.get, options.pop) were resolved by structural reading and flagged as uncertainties rather than asserted. The template filter/test/global families were merged into one group since they are structurally identical. Property getter/setter pairs, overload stubs, and trivial accessors were folded into their owning units.
